mil3.3.6:1.4: “It is the soul inside, venerable sir, that sees a visible form with the eye, hears a sound with the ear, smells an odor with the nose, tastes a flavor with the tongue, touches a touch with the body, and knows an idea with the mind—just as we, sitting here in the palace, can see through whichever window we want to look through: we could see through the east window, through the west window, through the north window, and through the south window.
mil3.3.6:1.5: In the same way, venerable sir, this soul inside sees through whichever door it wants to see through.”
mil3.3.6:2.2: “Great King, I will speak of the five doors; listen to that and pay close attention. If the soul inside sees a visible form with the eye, then just as we, sitting here in the palace, would see only a visible form through whichever window we want to look through—through the east window we would see only a visible form, through the west window only a visible form, through the north window only a visible form, through the south window only a visible form—so too by this soul inside, a visible form alone would have to be seen with the ear, a visible form alone with the nose, a visible form alone with the tongue, a visible form alone with the body, a visible form alone with the mind;
mil3.3.6:2.3: a sound alone would have to be heard with the eye, a sound alone with the nose, a sound alone with the tongue, a sound alone with the body, a sound alone with the mind;
mil3.3.6:2.4: an odor alone would have to be smelled with the eye, an odor alone with the ear, an odor alone with the tongue, an odor alone with the body, an odor alone with the mind;
mil3.3.6:2.5: a flavor alone would have to be tasted with the eye, a flavor alone with the ear, a flavor alone with the nose, a flavor alone with the body, a flavor alone with the mind;
mil3.3.6:2.6: a touch alone would have to be touched with the eye, a touch alone with the ear, a touch alone with the nose, a touch alone with the tongue, a touch alone with the mind;
mil3.3.6:2.7: an idea alone would have to be known with the eye, an idea alone with the ear, an idea alone with the nose, an idea alone with the tongue, an idea alone with the body?”
mil3.3.6:3.1: “It is not consistent for you, Great King, the later with the earlier, or the earlier with the later. Or again, Great King, just as we, sitting here in the palace, with these lattice windows opened, looking outward through the great open space, see a visible form much better, so too by this soul inside, with the doors of the eyes opened, a visible form should be seen much better through the great open space; with the ears opened … with the nose opened … with the tongue opened … with the body opened, through the great open space a sound should be heard much better, an odor smelled, a flavor tasted, a touch touched?”
mil3.3.6:4.1: “It is not consistent for you, Great King, the later with the earlier, or the earlier with the later. Or again, Great King, suppose this Dinna were to go out and stand in the outer gateway; would you know, Great King: ‘This Dinna has gone out and is standing in the outer gateway’?”
mil3.3.6:4.3: “Or again, Great King, suppose this Dinna were to come inside and stand before you; would you know, Great King: ‘This Dinna has come inside and is standing before me’?”
mil3.3.6:4.5: “In the same way, Great King, when a flavor is placed on the tongue, would that soul inside know sourness, saltiness, bitterness, pungency, astringency, or sweetness?”
mil3.3.6:4.7: “When those flavors have entered inside, would he know sourness, saltiness, bitterness, pungency, astringency, or sweetness?”
mil3.3.6:5.1: “It is not consistent for you, Great King, the later with the earlier, or the earlier with the later. Suppose, Great King, a certain man were to have a hundred pots of honey brought, fill a honey trough, cover a man’s mouth, and throw him into the honey trough. Would that man know, Great King, whether the honey was good or not?”
mil3.3.6:5.4: “Because, venerable sir, no honey has entered his mouth.”
mil3.3.6:6.1: “It is not consistent for you, Great King, the later with the earlier, or the earlier with the later.”
mil3.3.6:6.2: “I am not able to converse with a debater like you;
mil3.3.6:7.1: Then the elder brought King Milinda to understand with a talk connected with the Abhidhamma—
mil3.3.6:7.2: “Here, Great King, dependent on the eye and visible forms, eye consciousness arises; born together with it are contact, feeling, perception, intention, unification of mind, the life faculty, and application of mind—thus these phenomena arise from conditions, and in this no experiencer is found; and dependent on the ear and sounds …
mil3.3.6:7.3: and dependent on the mind and ideas, mind consciousness arises; born together with it are contact, feeling, perception, intention, unification of mind, the life faculty, and application of mind—thus these phenomena arise from conditions, and in this no experiencer is found.”
